intervention.revisedText: Maya walked into the room. She counted the IV drips first—three steady, one fluctuating. The antiseptic smell mixed with something sweet she couldn't place. Her eyes automatically scanned the dosage labels on the cabinets: 5mg, 10mg, 20mg. The room was familiar; she'd counted these same tiles—127 of them—since Papa's diagnosis. She noted the 4:15am time on the clock. Three hours until her shift ended. She kept counting the pills in the dispenser, thirteen left, and determined to make it through without checking her phone.
